mode.title: Mode
mode.description: "List" browses ARCE's public OCDS RSS feed -- either the latest 500 release events platform-wide, or every release event published in one calendar month. "Detail" fetches the full merged tender/buyer/award record for one or more specific purchases (idCompra).

year.title: Year (mode=list only, optional)
year.description: Restrict the list to one calendar month's release events. Must be given together with 'month' -- ARCE's own feed 404s on year-only. Leave both blank to get the latest 500 release events across the whole platform instead.

month.title: Month 1-12 (mode=list only, optional)
month.description: Restrict the list to one calendar month's release events. Must be given together with 'year'.

maxResults.title: Max results (mode=list only)
maxResults.description: Caps how many release-event rows this run returns. A single month's feed is not paged upstream and commonly carries several thousand events, so this cap is applied client-side after fetching.

fetchDetail.title: Fetch full merged detail for each list row (mode=list only)
fetchDetail.description: When enabled, each list row is enriched with the same merged tender/buyer/award summary fields and full 'releases' history as mode=detail -- one or more extra requests per row, so runs take longer.

idCompra.title: Purchase ID -- idCompra (mode=detail only)
idCompra.description: A single purchase's ARCE identifier, e.g. 1314718. Also accepts a full ocid (ocds-yfs5dr-1314718). Find idCompra values from a 'list' mode run's idCompra field.

idCompras.title: Purchase IDs -- idCompras (mode=detail only)
idCompras.description: Multiple idCompra values (or ocids) to fetch full detail for in one run.

maxConcurrency.title: Max concurrent workers (mode=detail only)
maxConcurrency.description: How many purchase lookups to run in parallel.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Apify Proxy configuration. Residential is on by default. No WAF or geo-block was observed on this target during recon (plain HTTP requests succeeded with no TLS impersonation needed), so a direct connection is also expected to work.
